Net per patient = 0.5 x the Part D figure a beneficiary above ($5,700.19 in 2024, $6,083.17 in 2025): $2,850.09 and $3,041.58. Stock: 105,539 and 105,939. At this file's 50.30% stopping, 49.70% remain, so 2025 new starts are 105,939 - 105,539 x 0.4970 = 53,487. The pool is 10,550,000 x 0.70 = 7,385,000 eligible, less the 105,539 on Multaq, plus 700,000 eligible diagnoses (1,000,000 x 0.70) = 7,979,461. Capture: 53,487 / 7,979,461 = 0.670%, which is the anchor (0.735% without the year's diagnoses). CROSS-CHECK: the revenue basis counts 1.46 Multaq patients per 2025 Part D beneficiary (105,939 against 72,363), plausible for a drug of older patients; and 2,977 of 143,281 newly diagnosed adults (2.1%) started dronedarone within 90 days (Kipp et al. 2024). MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT: parity with Multaq, 1.0 x 0.670% = 0.67%. For more: a first-in-class mechanism in a class of old drugs, and Novartis already sells Entresto and Leqvio to cardiologists. Against: the evidence is a 165-patient Phase 2 on a surrogate endpoint that has not read out; generic antiarrhythmics took 91% of first starts against dronedarone's 8% (Tardos et al. 2021); and 9.5% of antiarrhythmic starters had a catheter ablation within two years (Kipp et al. 2024), the non-drug route to the same rhythm control
